summary: Tested P0 login fix (5 users) and P1 role-based access (data_entry, employee). Backend tests: 15/15 PASS. Frontend tests: 6/7 PASS — found CRITICAL bug: App.js imports Products from ProductsEnhanced.js, but main agent edited /app/frontend/src/pages/Products.js. So the data_entry hide-check on Attachments was applied to the WRONG file. Admin also does not see the Attachments section (it doesn't exist in ProductsEnhanced.js).

ui_bugs.issue: App.js routes to ProductsEnhanced.js (line 16: `import Products from './pages/ProductsEnhanced';`) — but the role-based hide for Attachments was added to /app/frontend/src/pages/Products.js (lines 482-495). ProductsEnhanced.js has no Attachments section and no data_entry role check at all. Result: admin user does NOT see an Attachments upload section (regression for admin); data_entry hides nothing because nothing was there to begin with (test passes coincidentally).

rca of the issue: Root cause: App.js imports `Products` from `./pages/ProductsEnhanced` (line 16). The fix described in the review request was applied to /app/frontend/src/pages/Products.js — a stale/unused file. Reproduction: curl http://localhost:3000/static/js/bundle.js | grep -c 'product-attachments-section' → 0; grep -c 'Assign Serials' → 1 (proves ProductsEnhanced is in bundle, Products.js is not). Mitigation: re-apply the data_entry attachments hide-check inside ProductsEnhanced.js OR switch the App.js import to Products and reconcile differences.
